description: A large evergreen tree 10-25 m tall with glossy, leathery, oval leaves, clusters of small fragrant whitish flowers and oblong fruits that ripen from green to purple-black with a sweet-astringent taste that stains the tongue.
cultural_significance: India is called Jambudvipa in Puranic geography, named after the Jambu tree. The fruit is a beloved summer fruit. Prominent in the epics, Puranas and Nighantus.
habitat: Moist tropical lowlands, riverbanks and forests of the Indian subcontinent; widely planted as a shade and avenue tree.

uses.title: Diabetes support
uses.detail: Seed powder is the best-known traditional remedy for Madhumeha (diabetes), and the fruit is described as supportive in excess urination.

uses.title: Diarrhoea and dysentery
uses.detail: Bark decoction and fruit juice are astringent and are traditionally used in loose stools.

uses.title: Mouth and throat care
uses.detail: Bark decoction is traditionally used as a gargle for mouth ulcers, sore throat and bleeding gums.

uses.title: Digestive tonic
uses.detail: Fruit with black salt is traditionally eaten as a digestive in summer.

uses.title: Blood sugar research
uses.detail: Jamboline and anthocyanins in seeds have been studied for glucose-lowering effects; evidence is mixed.

preparations.name: Seed powder (beeja churna)
preparations.method: Wash and dry seeds, then grind to fine powder; taken with water.
preparations.note: Used traditionally in diabetes; people on medication must consult a doctor.

preparations.name: Fruit juice or fresh fruit
preparations.method: Eat ripe fruit or press the juice, often with a pinch of black salt.
preparations.note: Avoid with milk or on an empty stomach in some traditions.

preparations.name: Bark decoction
preparations.method: Boil bark in water and strain; use as a gargle or small sip.

preparations.name: Jamun vinegar
preparations.method: Fermented fruit juice used as a digestive tonic.

precautions: May lower blood sugar, so people on diabetes medicines, especially those using insulin, should consult a doctor and monitor glucose. Stop before scheduled surgery. Excess fruit can cause constipation, throat irritation or Vata aggravation. Traditionally avoid with milk on an empty stomach.

cultivation.soil: Deep, moist, well-drained loam; tolerates waterlogging
cultivation.water: Moderate to high; thrives near water
cultivation.propagation: Seeds or grafting; grafted trees fruit earlier
cultivation.harvest: Fruits ripen in the monsoon, June to August

fun_fact: Eating jamun turns the tongue purple, and the tree's ancient name Jambu gave India its Puranic name Jambudvipa.

regions.name: Western Ghats
regions.note: Native in evergreen and moist deciduous forests
